verses.1:1: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, a called apostle, set apart for the Gospel of God,
verses.1:2: which He had promised beforehand through His prophets in the holy Scriptures
verses.1:3: concerning His Son, who was made for Him from the seed of David according to the flesh,
verses.1:4: who was predestined as the Son of God in power according to the Spirit of sanctification from the resurrection of the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,
verses.1:5: through whom we have received grace and apostleship for obedience to the faith among all the nations for the sake of His name,
verses.1:6: among whom you also are the called of Jesus Christ:
verses.1:7: to all who are in Rome, beloved by God, called saints. Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:8: First, I give thanks to my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed throughout the entire world.
verses.1:9: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Gospel of His Son, that unceasingly I make mention of you
verses.1:10: always in my prayers, imploring that somehow at long last I may have a prosperous journey in the will of God to come to you.
verses.1:11: For I long to see you, so that I may impart to you some spiritual grace to strengthen you,
verses.1:12: that is, to be comforted together among you through the faith that is mutual, both yours and mine.
verses.1:13: Now I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that I have often planned to come to you (and have been prevented until now), so that I may have some fruit among you also, just as among the rest of the nations.
verses.1:14: To Greeks and to barbarians, to the wise and to the foolish, I am a debtor;
verses.1:15: so, as far as lies in me, I am ready to proclaim the Gospel to you also who are in Rome.
verses.1:16: For I am not ashamed of the Gospel. For it is God's power for salvation to every believer, to the Jew first and to the Greek.
verses.1:17: For the righteousness of God is revealed in it from faith to faith, just as it is written: "But the righteous one lives by faith."
verses.1:18: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of those men who hold back the truth of God in unrighteousness,
verses.1:19: because what is known of God is evident in them. For God has made it evident to them.
verses.1:20: For His invisible realities, from the creation of the world, are clearly perceived, being understood through the things that have been made, His everlasting power also and His divinity, so that they are without excuse.
verses.1:21: Because although they had known God, they did not glorify Him as God or give thanks, but they became empty in their thoughts, and their foolish heart was darkened.
verses.1:22: For claiming themselves to be wise, they became fools.
verses.1:23: And they changed the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, of four-footed creatures, and of reptiles.
verses.1:24: For this reason God handed them over to the desires of their heart, to impurity, so that they dishonor their own bodies in themselves,
verses.1:25: who traded the truth of God for a lie, and revered and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed throughout the ages. Amen.
verses.1:26: Therefore God handed them over to passions of disgrace; for their females changed the natural use into that use which is contrary to nature.
verses.1:27: Likewise also the males, leaving the natural use of the female, burned in their desires toward one another, males committing indecency with males, and receiving in themselves the recompense for their error that was due.
verses.1:28: And just as they did not approve of having God in their knowledge, God handed them over to a reprobate mind, so that they do the things that are not fitting,
verses.1:29: being filled with all iniquity, malice, fornication, greed, wickedness; full of envy, murder, contention, deceit, spitefulness; whisperers,
verses.1:30: slanderers, hateful to God, insolent, proud, haughty, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
verses.1:31: foolish, disorderly, without affection, without fidelity, without mercy.
verses.1:32: Although they had known the righteousness of God, they did not understand that those who practice such things are worthy of death, and not only those who do them, but also those who consent to those who do them.
verses.2:1: For this reason you are without excuse, man, everyone who judges. For in what you judge another, you condemn yourself, for you practice the same things that you judge.
verses.2:2: For we know that the judgment of God is according to truth against those who practice such things.
verses.2:3: Now do you suppose this, man, you who judge those who practice such things and do them, that you will escape the judgment of God?
verses.2:4: Or do you despise the riches of His goodness, and patience, and longsuffering? Are you unaware that the kindness of God leads you to repentance?
verses.2:5: But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and of the revelation of the righteous judgment of God,
verses.2:6: who will repay each one according to his works:
verses.2:7: to those indeed who according to patience in good work seek glory, and honor, and incorruption, eternal life;
verses.2:8: but to those who act from contention and who do not assent to the truth, but trust in iniquity, wrath and indignation.
verses.2:9: Tribulation and distress upon every soul of man who works evil, of the Jew first and of the Greek;
verses.2:10: but glory, and honor, and peace to everyone who works good, to the Jew first and to the Greek;
verses.2:11: for there is no favoritism with God.
verses.2:12: For all who have sinned without the law will perish without the law, and all who have sinned in the law will be judged by the law.
verses.2:13: For the hearers of the law are not righteous before God, but the doers of the law will be justified.
verses.2:14: Now when Gentiles, who do not have the law, naturally do the things of the law, such people, not having the law, are a law to themselves;
verses.2:15: who show the work of the law written in their hearts, their own conscience bearing witness to them, and their thoughts between themselves accusing or even defending them,
verses.2:16: on the day when God will judge the hidden things of men, according to my Gospel, through Jesus Christ.
verses.2:17: But if you bear the name of a Jew, and rest in the law, and boast in God,
verses.2:18: and know His will, and approve the things that are more profitable, being instructed through the law,
verses.2:19: you are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light to those who are in darkness,
verses.2:20: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, having the form of knowledge and of truth in the law.
verses.2:21: You, therefore, who teach another, do not teach yourself; you who preach that one must not steal, you steal;
verses.2:22: you who say that one must not commit adultery, you commit adultery; you who abhor idols, you commit sacrilege;
verses.2:23: you who boast in the law, through transgression of the law you dishonor God.
verses.2:24: (For the name of God is blasphemed through you among the nations, as it is written.)
verses.2:25: Circumcision indeed is beneficial if you observe the law; but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
verses.2:26: If, therefore, the uncircumcised one keeps the righteous ordinances of the law, will not his uncircumcision be counted as circumcision?
verses.2:27: And will that which is uncircumcision by nature, fulfilling the law, judge you, who through the letter and circumcision are a transgressor of the law?
verses.2:28: For he is not a Jew who is one in what is manifest, nor is that circumcision which is manifest in the flesh;
verses.2:29: but he is a Jew who is one in secret, and circumcision is of the heart, in spirit, not in letter; whose praise is not from men, but from God.
verses.3:1: What more, then, does the Jew have? Or what is the benefit of circumcision?
verses.3:2: Much in every way. First indeed, because the utterances of God were entrusted to them.
verses.3:3: For what if some of them did not believe? Will their unbelief nullify the faithfulness of God? Far from it!
verses.3:4: But God is true, while every person is a liar, just as it is written: "So that You may be justified in Your words, and prevail when You are judged."
verses.3:5: But if our unrighteousness commends the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous, who inflicts wrath?
verses.3:6: I speak in human terms. Far from it! Otherwise, how will God judge this world?
verses.3:7: For if the truth of God has abounded through my lie to His glory, why am I also still judged as a sinner?
verses.3:8: And why not (as we are slandered, and as some claim we say), "Let us do evil so that good may come"? Their condemnation is just.
verses.3:9: What then? Do we surpass them? Not at all. For we have charged that Jews and Greeks are all under sin,
verses.3:10: just as it is written: "There is no righteous person;
verses.3:11: there is no one who understands; there is no one who seeks God.
verses.3:12: All have turned aside; together they have become useless. There is no one who does good; there is not even one.
verses.3:13: An open tomb is their throat; with their tongues they acted deceitfully; the venom of asps is under their lips,
verses.3:14: whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness;
verses.3:15: their feet are swift to shed blood;
verses.3:16: ruin and misery are in their ways,
verses.3:17: and the way of peace they have not known;
verses.3:18: there is no fear of God before their eyes."
verses.3:19: Now we know that whatever the law speaks, it speaks to those who are in the law, so that every mouth may be stopped and the whole world may become subject to God,
verses.3:20: because by works of the law no flesh will be justified before Him. For through the law comes the knowledge of sin.
verses.3:21: But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been manifested, attested by the law and the prophets,
verses.3:22: namely, the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ, to all and upon all who believe in Him; for there is no distinction,
verses.3:23: for all have sinned and lack the glory of God,
verses.3:24: being justified freely through His grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,
verses.3:25: whom God set forth as a propitiation through faith in His blood, for the demonstration of His righteousness because of the remission of previous offenses,
verses.3:26: in the forbearance of God, for the demonstration of His righteousness at this time, so that He Himself may be righteous and may justify him who is of faith in Jesus Christ.
verses.3:27: Where then is your boasting? It is excluded. Through what law? Of deeds? No, but through the law of faith.
verses.3:28: For we consider that a person is justified through faith apart from works of the law.
verses.3:29: Or is God the God of the Jews only? Is He not of the Gentiles also? Yes, of the Gentiles also,
verses.3:30: since indeed God is one, who justifies the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith.
verses.3:31: Do we then destroy the law through faith? Far from it! Rather, we establish the law.
verses.4:1: What then shall we say that Abraham, our father according to the flesh, has found?
verses.4:2: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has glory, but not before God.
verses.4:3: For what does Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness."
verses.4:4: Now to the one who works, the wage is not counted according to grace, but according to debt.
verses.4:5: But to the one who does not work, yet believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is reckoned for righteousness according to the purpose of the grace of God.
verses.4:6: Just as David also speaks of the blessedness of the person to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:
verses.4:7: "Blessed are those whose iniquities have been forgiven, and whose sins have been covered.
verses.4:8: Blessed is the man to whom the Lord has not counted sin."
verses.4:9: Does this blessedness, then, remain in circumcision only, or also in uncircumcision? For we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.
verses.4:10: How then was it reckoned? In circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.
verses.4:11: And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith that is in uncircumcision, so that he might be the father of all who believe while in uncircumcision, so that it might be reckoned to them also for righteousness,
verses.4:12: and that he might be the father of circumcision, not only to those who are of circumcision, but also to those who follow the footsteps of the faith that is in the uncircumcision of our father Abraham.
verses.4:13: For the promise to Abraham or to his offspring, that he would be heir of the world, was not through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
verses.4:14: For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith has been made void; the promise has been abolished.
verses.4:15: For the law produces wrath. For where there is no law, neither is there transgression.
verses.4:16: Therefore it is by faith, so that according to grace the promise may be firm to all the offspring, not only to the one who is of the law, but also to the one who is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all
verses.4:17: (just as it is written: "I have appointed you a father of many nations") before God, whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls the things that are not as the things that are.
verses.4:18: Against hope, he believed in hope, so that he might become the father of many nations, according to what had been spoken to him: "So will your offspring be."
verses.4:19: And he did not grow weak in faith, nor did he consider his own body dead, when he was already nearly a hundred years old, or the dead womb of Sarah.
verses.4:20: Moreover, at the promise of God he did not waver in distrust, but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God,
verses.4:21: knowing most fully that whatever He had promised, He is also able to do.
verses.4:22: Therefore it was also reckoned to him for righteousness.
verses.4:23: Now it was not written for his sake alone that it was reckoned to him for righteousness,
verses.4:24: but also for our sake, to whom it will be reckoned as those who believe in Him who raised Jesus Christ our Lord from the dead,
verses.4:25: who was handed over for our offenses, and rose again for our justification.
verses.5:1: Justified by faith, therefore, let us have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.5:2: through whom we also have access through faith into this grace in which we stand, and we boast in the hope of the glory of the sons of God.
verses.5:3: And not only that, but we also boast in afflictions, knowing that affliction produces endurance;
verses.5:4: and endurance, proven worth; and proven worth, hope;
verses.5:5: and hope does not put to shame, because the love of God is poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us.
verses.5:6: For why did Christ, while we were still weak, die at the appointed time for the ungodly?
verses.5:7: For scarcely does anyone die for a righteous person; yet for a good person someone might perhaps dare to die.
verses.5:8: But God commends His own love in us, because while we were still sinners, at the appointed time,
verses.5:9: Christ died for us. Much more, therefore, now justified in His blood, we will be saved from wrath through Him.
verses.5:10: For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son, much more, having been reconciled, will we be saved in His life.
verses.5:11: And not only that, but we also boast in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.
verses.5:12: For this reason, just as through one man sin entered into this world, and through sin death, and so death passed through to all people, in whom all sinned.
verses.5:13: For until the law, sin was in the world, yet sin was not charged when there was no law.
verses.5:14: Yet death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the likeness of the transgression of Adam, who is a pattern of the One to come.
verses.5:15: But the gift is not like the offense: for if by the offense of one many died, much more have the grace of God and the gift in the grace of the one man Jesus Christ abounded toward many.
verses.5:16: And the gift is not as it was through one sin. For judgment indeed is from one to condemnation, whereas grace is from many offenses to justification.
verses.5:17: For if by the offense of one, death reigned through the one, much more will those who receive the abundance of grace, and of the gift, and of righteousness reign in life through the one, Jesus Christ.
verses.5:18: Therefore, just as through the offense of one it came upon all people to condemnation, so also through the righteousness of one it comes upon all people to justification of life.
verses.5:19: For just as through the disobedience of one man many were constituted sinners, so also through the obedience of one many will be constituted righteous.
verses.5:20: Now the law came in alongside so that the offense might abound. Yet where the offense abounded, grace superabounded,
verses.5:21: so that just as sin reigned to death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to eternal life, through Jesus Christ our Lord.
verses.6:1: What, then, will we say? Will we remain in sin so that grace may abound?
verses.6:2: Far from it. For we who died to sin, how will we still live in it?
verses.6:3: Or are you unaware that all of us who were baptized in Christ Jesus were baptized in His death?
verses.6:4: For we were buried together with Him through baptism into death, so that just as Christ rose from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.
verses.6:5: For if we have become planted together in the likeness of His death, we will likewise be so in that of His resurrection,
verses.6:6: knowing this, that our old man was crucified together with Him, so that the body of sin might be destroyed, and we might no longer serve sin.
verses.6:7: For the one who has died has been justified from sin.
verses.6:8: Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live together with Christ,
verses.6:9: knowing that Christ, rising from the dead, no longer dies; death will no longer have mastery over Him.
verses.6:10: For in dying to sin, He died once; yet in living, He lives to God.
verses.6:11: In the same way, consider yourselves also to be dead indeed to sin, yet living to God, in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.6:12: Therefore, let sin not reign in your mortal body so that you obey its cravings.
verses.6:13: And do not present your members as weapons of iniquity to sin, but present yourselves to God as those living from the dead, and your members as weapons of righteousness to God.
verses.6:14: For sin will not have mastery over you, for you are not under law, but under grace.
verses.6:15: What then? Will we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? Far from it.
verses.6:16: Do you not know that to whomever you present yourselves as slaves for obedience, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, whether of sin to death, or of obedience to righteousness?
verses.6:17: Now thanks be to God that you were slaves of sin, yet you obeyed from the heart that pattern of teaching into which you were delivered.
verses.6:18: And freed from sin, you were made slaves of righteousness.
verses.6:19: I speak in a human way because of the weakness of your flesh: for just as you presented your members to serve impurity and iniquity leading to iniquity, so now present your members to serve righteousness leading to sanctification.
verses.6:20: For when you were slaves of sin, you were free from righteousness.
verses.6:21: What fruit, then, did you have at that time in those things over which you are now ashamed? For their end is death.
verses.6:22: Now, however, freed from sin and made slaves to God, you have your fruit leading to sanctification, and as the end, eternal life.
verses.6:23: For the pay of sin is death. Yet the grace of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.7:1: Or are you unaware, brothers (for I am speaking to those who know the law), that the law has mastery over a person for as long as he lives?
verses.7:2: For a woman who is under a husband is bound to the law while her husband lives; yet if her husband dies, she is released from the law of the husband.
verses.7:3: Therefore, while her husband lives, she will be called an adulteress if she is with another man; yet if her husband dies, she is freed from the law of the husband, so that she is not an adulteress if she is with another man.
verses.7:4: So then, my brothers, you also have been put to death to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another, to Him who rose from the dead, in order that we may bear fruit for God.
verses.7:5: For while we were in the flesh, the passions of sins, which were through the law, were at work in our members so that they might bear fruit for death.
verses.7:6: Now, however, we have been released from the law of death, in which we were held, so that we may serve in newness of spirit, and not in oldness of the letter.
verses.7:7: What, then, will we say? Is the law sin? Far from it. Yet I did not know sin except through the law; for I would not have known coveting if the law had not said, "You shall not covet."
verses.7:8: Yet seizing an opportunity, sin produced all coveting in me through the commandment. For without the law, sin was dead.
verses.7:9: Now I was once alive without the law, but when the commandment came, sin lived again.
verses.7:10: I, however, died; and the commandment that was for life—this very one was found by me to be for death.
verses.7:11: For sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, led me astray, and through it killed me.
verses.7:12: So then, the law indeed is holy, and the commandment is holy, and righteous, and good.
verses.7:13: Did what is good, then, become death to me? Far from it. Rather, sin, so that it might appear to be sin, produced death for me through what is good, so that sin might become sinful beyond measure through the commandment.
verses.7:14: For we know that the law is spiritual, whereas I am fleshly, sold under sin.
verses.7:15: For what I carry out, I do not understand: for the good that I want, this I do not practice; rather, the evil that I hate, that I do.
verses.7:16: Now if I do that which I do not want, I concur with the law that it is good.
verses.7:17: Now, however, it is no longer I who carry it out, but the sin that dwells in me.
verses.7:18: For I know that good does not dwell in me, that is, in my flesh. For to will is at hand for me, yet how to accomplish the good I do not find.
verses.7:19: For the good that I want, this I do not do; rather, the evil that I do not want, this I practice.
verses.7:20: Now if I do that which I do not want, it is no longer I who carry it out, but the sin that dwells in me.
verses.7:21: I find, therefore, a law, that for me, wanting to do good, evil is at hand;
verses.7:22: for I take delight in the law of God according to the inner man,
verses.7:23: yet I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind and taking me captive in the law of sin that is in my members.
verses.7:24: Miserable man that I am, who will free me from the body of this death?
verses.7:25: The grace of God, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Therefore, I myself with the mind serve the law of God, yet with the flesh, the law of sin.
verses.8:1: So then, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus, who do not walk according to the flesh.
verses.8:2: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has freed me from the law of sin and death.
verses.8:3: For what was impossible for the Law, in that it was weakened through the flesh—God, by sending His own Son in the likeness of the flesh of sin and concerning sin, condemned sin in the flesh,
verses.8:4: so that the righteous requirement of the Law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
verses.8:5: For those who are according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, while those who are according to the Spirit set their thoughts on the things of the Spirit.
verses.8:6: For the mindset of the flesh is death, but the mindset of the Spirit is life and peace;
verses.8:7: because the wisdom of the flesh is hostile to God; for it is not subject to the law of God, nor indeed can it be.
verses.8:8: Now those who are in the flesh are not able to please God.
verses.8:9: You, however, are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you. Yet if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, this person does not belong to Him.
verses.8:10: Now if Christ is in you, the body indeed is dead because of sin, while the spirit is alive because of justification.
verses.8:11: And if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, He who raised Jesus Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies because of His Spirit who dwells in you.
verses.8:12: Therefore, brothers, we are debtors not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh.
verses.8:13: For if you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the flesh, you will live.
verses.8:14: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God.
verses.8:15: For you have not received a spirit of slavery again in fear, but you have received a Spirit of adoption as sons, in whom we cry out, "Abba (Father)."
verses.8:16: For the Spirit Himself bears witness to our spirit that we are sons of God.
verses.8:17: And if sons, also heirs: heirs indeed of God, and fellow heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with Him so that we may also be glorified with Him.
verses.8:18: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the coming glory that will be revealed in us.
verses.8:19: For the eager expectation of creation awaits the revelation of the sons of God.
verses.8:20: For creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but because of Him who subjected it in hope,
verses.8:21: because creation itself will also be freed from the slavery of corruption into the freedom of the glory of the sons of God.
verses.8:22: For we know that all creation groans and suffers the pains of childbirth even until now.
verses.8:23: And not only creation, but we ourselves also, having the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we groan within ourselves, awaiting adoption as sons of God, the redemption of our body.
verses.8:24: For in hope we were saved. Now hope that is seen is not hope; for what someone sees, why does he hope for it?
verses.8:25: Yet if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with patience.
verses.8:26: And likewise the Spirit also helps our weakness; for we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit Himself pleads for us with inexpressible groanings.
verses.8:27: And the One who searches hearts knows what the Spirit desires, because He pleads for the saints according to God.
verses.8:28: And we know that for those who love God, all things work together toward good, for those who according to His purpose have been called as saints.
verses.8:29: For those whom He foreknew, He also predestined to become conformed to the image of His Son, so that He Himself might be the firstborn among many brothers.
verses.8:30: And those whom He predestined, these He also called; and those whom He called, these He also justified; and those whom He justified, those He also glorified.
verses.8:31: What then will we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
verses.8:32: He who did not spare even His own Son, but handed Him over for us all, how has He not also freely given us all things with Him?
verses.8:33: Who will bring a charge against God's chosen ones? It is God who justifies;
verses.8:34: who is there to condemn? It is Christ Jesus, who died, or rather who also rose again, who is at the right hand of God, who also intercedes for us.
verses.8:35: Who then will separate us from the love of Christ? Tribulation, or distress, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or persecution, or sword?
verses.8:36: (Just as it is written: "For Your sake we are put to death all day long; we have been reckoned like sheep for slaughter.")
verses.8:37: Yet in all these things we overcome because of Him who loved us.
verses.8:38: For I am convinced that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor might,
verses.8:39: nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.9:1: I speak the truth in Christ; I do not lie, with my conscience bearing witness to me in the Holy Spirit,
verses.9:2: that I have great sorrow and continual pain in my heart.
verses.9:3: For I myself could wish to be accursed from Christ for my brothers, who are my relatives according to the flesh,
verses.9:4: who are Israelites, whose is the adoption of sons, and the glory, and the covenant, and the lawgiving, and the worship, and the promises;
verses.9:5: whose are the fathers, and from whom is Christ according to the flesh, who is God above all things, blessed forever. Amen.
verses.9:6: It is not, however, that the word of God has failed. For not all who are from Israel are Israelites;
verses.9:7: nor are those who are the offspring of Abraham all sons; rather, "In Isaac your offspring will be called."
verses.9:8: That is, it is not those who are sons of the flesh who are sons of God, but those who are sons of the promise are reckoned as offspring.
verses.9:9: For the word of promise is this: "At this time I will come, and Sarah will have a son."
verses.9:10: And not only she, but Rebekah also, having conceived from one union with our father Isaac.
verses.9:11: For when they had not yet been born, or done anything good or bad (so that God's purpose according to election might remain),
verses.9:12: not from works, but from Him who calls, it was said to her, "The older will serve the younger,"
verses.9:13: just as it is written: "I have loved Jacob, but I have hated Esau."
verses.9:14: What then will we say? Is there injustice with God? Certainly not!
verses.9:15: For He says to Moses, "I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will grant mercy to whom I will be merciful."
verses.9:16: Therefore it does not depend on the one who wills, nor on the one who runs, but on God who shows mercy.
verses.9:17: For Scripture says to Pharaoh, "For this very reason I have raised you up, so that I may show My power in you, and so that My name may be declared throughout all the earth."
verses.9:18: So then He has mercy on whom He wills, and whom He wills He hardens.
verses.9:19: You say to me then, "Why does He still find fault? For who resists His will?"
verses.9:20: Man, who are you to reply to God? Does the thing formed say to the one who formed it, "Why did you make me like this?"
verses.9:21: Or does the potter not have authority over the clay to make from the same lump one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?
verses.9:22: What if God, desiring to show wrath and to make known His power, endured with great patience vessels of wrath fitted for destruction,
verses.9:23: so that He might show the riches of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared in advance for glory,
verses.9:24: even us, whom He also called, not only from the Jews, but also among the Gentiles?
verses.9:25: Just as He says in Hosea, "I will call those who are not My people, 'My people,' and her who is not beloved, 'Beloved,' and her who has not obtained mercy, 'One who has obtained mercy.'"
verses.9:26: "And it will be: in the place where it was said to them, 'You are not My people,' there they will be called sons of the living God."
verses.9:27: And Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: "Even if the number of the sons of Israel is like the sand of the sea, a remnant will be saved.
verses.9:28: For He is completing the word and cutting it short in equity, because the Lord will carry out a shortened word upon the earth."
verses.9:29: And as Isaiah foretold: "If the Lord Sabaoth had not left us offspring, we would have become like Sodom, and we would have been similar to Gomorrah."
verses.9:30: What then will we say? That Gentiles, who were not pursuing righteousness, laid hold of righteousness, namely, the righteousness that is from faith;
verses.9:31: whereas Israel, in pursuing the law of righteousness, did not reach the law of righteousness.
verses.9:32: Why? Because it was not from faith, but as if from works; for they stumbled against the stone of stumbling,
verses.9:33: just as it is written: "Look, I place in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, and everyone who believes in Him will not be brought to shame."
verses.10:1: Brothers, my heart's desire indeed, and my supplication to God, is made on their behalf for salvation.
verses.10:2: For I bear witness concerning them that they have zeal for God, yet not according to knowledge.
verses.10:3: For, not knowing God's righteousness and seeking to set up their own, they have not submitted to God's righteousness.
verses.10:4: For the end of the law is Christ, for righteousness to everyone who believes.
verses.10:5: For Moses wrote that the person who does the righteousness that is from the law will live by it.
verses.10:6: But the righteousness that is from faith speaks in this way: "Do not say in your heart, 'Who will ascend into heaven?' (that is, to bring Christ down),
verses.10:7: or, 'Who will descend into the abyss?'" (that is, to call Christ back from the dead).
verses.10:8: But what does Scripture say? "The word is near, in your mouth and in your heart." That is the word of faith that we preach.
verses.10:9: Because if you confess the Lord Jesus with your mouth, and believe in your heart that God has raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.
verses.10:10: For with the heart one believes for righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made for salvation.
verses.10:11: For Scripture says, "Everyone who believes in Him will not be brought to shame."
verses.10:12: For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; for the same Lord of all is rich toward all who call upon Him.
verses.10:13: For everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.
verses.10:14: How then will they call upon Him in whom they have not believed? Or how will they believe Him whom they have not heard? And how will they hear without someone preaching?
verses.10:15: And how will they preach unless they are sent? Just as it is written: "How beautiful are the feet of those who proclaim good news of peace, of those who proclaim good news of good things!"
verses.10:16: Yet not all obey the gospel. For Isaiah says, "Lord, who has believed our report?"
verses.10:17: Therefore faith is from hearing, and hearing is through the word of Christ.
verses.10:18: But I say: Have they not heard? Yes indeed: "Into all the earth their sound has gone out, and to the ends of the world their words."
verses.10:19: But I say: Did Israel not know? First Moses says, "I will lead you to jealousy by what is not a nation; by a foolish nation I will drive you to anger."
verses.10:20: And Isaiah is bold and says, "I was found by those who were not seeking Me; I appeared openly to those who did not ask for Me."
verses.10:21: But to Israel he says, "All day long I have stretched out My hands to an unbelieving and contradicting people."
verses.11:1: I say then: Has God rejected His people? Far from it. For I also am an Israelite, from the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
verses.11:2: God has not rejected His people, whom He foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says in Elijah, how he appeals to God against Israel?
verses.11:3: "Lord, they have killed Your prophets, they have undermined Your altars, and I have been left alone, and they are seeking my life."
verses.11:4: But what does the divine response say to him? "I have left for Myself seven thousand men who have not bent their knees before Baal."
verses.11:5: So then, at this time also, a remnant has been saved according to the election of grace.
verses.11:6: Now if it is by grace, it is no longer from works; otherwise grace is no longer grace.
verses.11:7: What then? What Israel was seeking, this it did not obtain, but the election obtained it, while the rest were blinded,
verses.11:8: just as it is written: "God has given them a spirit of compunction, eyes so that they may not see, and ears so that they may not hear, down to this very day."
verses.11:9: And David says: "Let their table become a snare, and a trap, and a stumbling block, and a repayment to them.
verses.11:10: Let their eyes be darkened so that they may not see, and bend their back always."
verses.11:11: I say then: Did they stumble so that they would fall? Far from it. Rather, by their offense there is salvation for the Gentiles, so that they may emulate them.
verses.11:12: Now if their offense is the riches of the world, and their diminishment is the riches of the Gentiles, how much more their fullness?
verses.11:13: For to you Gentiles I speak: as long as I am indeed an apostle of the Gentiles, I will honor my ministry,
verses.11:14: if somehow I may provoke my flesh to emulation and save some of them.
verses.11:15: For if their loss is the reconciliation of the world, what will their reception be, except life from the dead?
verses.11:16: Now if the first portion is holy, so also is the lump; and if the root is holy, so also are the branches.
verses.11:17: Now if some of the branches were broken, and you, though you were a wild olive tree, were grafted in among them and became a sharer of the root and richness of the olive tree,
verses.11:18: do not boast against the branches. Now if you boast, you do not carry the root, but the root carries you.
verses.11:19: You will say then, "Branches were broken so that I might be grafted in."
verses.11:20: Well said: because of unbelief they were broken, while you stand by faith. Do not be haughty in mind, but fear.
verses.11:21: For if God did not spare the natural branches, perhaps He will not spare you either.
verses.11:22: See then the goodness and severity of God: toward those who fell, severity; but toward you, the goodness of God, if you remain in that goodness; otherwise you also will be cut off.
verses.11:23: And they also, if they do not remain in unbelief, will be grafted in, for God has the power to graft them in again.
verses.11:24: For if you were cut off from a natural wild olive tree and contrary to nature were grafted into a good olive tree, how much more will these, who are according to nature, be grafted into their own olive tree?
verses.11:25: For I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, brothers (so that you may not be wise to yourselves), that blindness in part has occurred in Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles should enter,
verses.11:26: and thus all Israel would be saved, just as it is written: "There will come out of Zion one who will deliver and turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
verses.11:27: And this is the covenant for them from Me, when I take away their sins."
verses.11:28: According to the gospel, indeed, they are enemies on your account; but according to election, they are most beloved on account of the fathers.
verses.11:29: For the gifts and calling of God are without regret.
verses.11:30: For just as you also formerly did not believe God, yet now have obtained mercy because of their unbelief,
verses.11:31: so now these also have not believed, for your mercy, so that they themselves may also obtain mercy.
verses.11:32: For God has confined all things in unbelief, so that He may have mercy on all.
verses.11:33: Oh, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God: how incomprehensible are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!
verses.11:34: For who has come to know the mind of the Lord? Or who was His counselor?
verses.11:35: Or who first gave to Him, and it will be repaid to him?
verses.11:36: Because from Him, and through Him, and in Him are all things; to Him be glory forever. Amen.
verses.12:1: Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercy of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing to God—your reasonable service.
verses.12:2: And do not be conformed to this age, but be reformed in the newness of your mind, so that you may discern what the will of God is: what is good, and well-pleasing, and perfect.
verses.12:3: For through the grace that has been given to me, I say to everyone among you not to think more highly than one ought to think, but to think with sober judgment, and to each person according as God has apportioned a measure of faith.
verses.12:4: For just as we have many members in one body, yet all the members do not have the same function,
verses.12:5: so we, being many, are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another.
verses.12:6: Now having differing gifts according to the grace that has been given to us: whether prophecy, in proportion to faith;
verses.12:7: or service, in serving; or the one who teaches, in teaching;
verses.12:8: the one who exhorts, in exhorting; the one who gives, in simplicity; the one who leads, in diligence; the one who shows mercy, in cheerfulness.
verses.12:9: Let love be without pretense: hating what is evil, clinging to what is good;
verses.12:10: loving one another with brotherly affection, outdoing one another in showing honor;
verses.12:11: not sluggish in diligence, fervent in spirit, serving the Lord;
verses.12:12: rejoicing in hope, patient in tribulation, steadfast in prayer;
verses.12:13: sharing in the needs of the saints, pursuing hospitality.
verses.12:14: Bless those who are persecuting you; bless, and do not curse.
verses.12:15: Rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep;
verses.12:16: being of the same mind toward one another; not setting your mind on lofty things, but associating with the lowly. Do not be wise in your own estimation;
verses.12:17: repaying no one evil for evil; taking care for what is honorable not only before God, but also before all people.
verses.12:18: If it can be done, as far as it depends on you, being at peace with all people;
verses.12:19: not avenging yourselves, dearly beloved, but leave room for wrath. For it is written: "Vengeance belongs to Me; I will repay," says the Lord.
verses.12:20: Rather, if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head.
verses.12:21: Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.
verses.13:1: Let every soul be subject to higher authorities, for there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been ordained by God.
verses.13:2: Therefore whoever resists authority resists God's ordinance; and those who resist acquire condemnation for themselves.
verses.13:3: For rulers are not a cause of fear for a good work, but for an evil one. Now do you want not to fear authority? Do what is good, and you will have praise from it,
verses.13:4: for it is God's servant to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid, for it does not carry the sword without cause; for it is God's servant, an avenger for wrath upon the one who does evil.
verses.13:5: Therefore be subject out of necessity, not only because of wrath, but also because of conscience.
verses.13:6: For on this account you also pay tribute, for they are God's servants, serving in this very matter.
verses.13:7: Render therefore to all what is owed: to whom tribute is owed, tribute; to whom revenue, revenue; to whom fear, fear; to whom honor, honor.
verses.13:8: Do not owe anyone anything, except to love one another; for whoever loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.
verses.13:9: For, "You shall not commit adultery; you shall not kill; you shall not steal; you shall not give false testimony; you shall not covet," and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
verses.13:10: Love of one's neighbor works no evil; therefore love is the fullness of the law.
verses.13:11: And this, knowing the time: that it is already the hour for us to rise from sleep. For our salvation is closer now than when we believed.
verses.13:12: The night has passed on, and the day has drawn near. Let us therefore cast aside the works of darkness and clothe ourselves with the armor of light.
verses.13:13: Let us walk honorably, as in the daytime: not in revelry and drunkenness, not in promiscuity and indecency, not in contention and rivalry,
verses.13:14: but clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not make provision for the flesh in its desires.
verses.14:1: Now receive the one who is weak in faith, not in disputes over thoughts.
verses.14:2: For one believes that he may eat all things; but let the one who is weak eat vegetables.
verses.14:3: Let the one who eats not scorn the one who does not eat, and let the one who does not eat not judge the one who eats, for God has received him.
verses.14:4: Who are you, who judge another's servant? To his own master he stands or falls; yet he will stand, for God is able to make him stand.
verses.14:5: For one judges between one day and another, while another judges every day; let each one abound in his own mind.
verses.14:6: The one who regards the day, for the Lord he regards it, and the one who eats, for the Lord he eats, for he gives thanks to God. And the one who does not eat, for the Lord he does not eat, and he gives thanks to God.
verses.14:7: For none of us lives for himself, and no one dies for himself.
verses.14:8: For whether we live, we live for the Lord, or whether we die, we die for the Lord. Therefore, whether we live or whether we die, we are the Lord's.
verses.14:9: For to this purpose Christ died and rose again, so that He might be Lord of both the dead and the living.
verses.14:10: But you, why do you judge your brother? Or you, why do you scorn your brother? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.
verses.14:11: For it is written: "As I live," says the Lord, "surely every knee will bow to Me, and every tongue will confess to God."
verses.14:12: Therefore, each one of us will render an account for himself to God.
verses.14:13: Therefore let us no longer judge one another, but rather make this your judgment: that you not place a stumbling block or a snare before a brother.
verses.14:14: I know and am confident in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean through Him; except to the one who considers something to be unclean, to him it is unclean.
verses.14:15: For if your brother is grieved because of food, you are no longer walking according to love. Do not by your food destroy the one for whom Christ died.
verses.14:16: Therefore, let our good not be slandered.
verses.14:17: For the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
verses.14:18: For the one who serves Christ in this pleases God and is approved by people.
verses.14:19: Therefore let us pursue the things of peace, and let us guard the things of edification toward one another.
verses.14:20: Do not destroy the work of God on account of food. Indeed, all things are clean, but it is evil for the person who eats with stumbling.
verses.14:21: It is good not to eat meat and not to drink wine, nor to do anything by which your brother stumbles, or is ensnared, or is weakened.
verses.14:22: Do you have faith? Keep it within yourself before God. Blessed is the one who does not judge himself in what he approves.
verses.14:23: But the one who makes a distinction, if he eats, is condemned, because it is not from faith. And everything that is not from faith is sin.
verses.15:1: Now we who are stronger ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
verses.15:2: Let each one of you please his neighbor for good, toward edification.
verses.15:3: For indeed Christ did not please Himself, but just as it is written: "The reproaches of those who reproach You fell upon Me."
verses.15:4: For whatever things were written were written for our teaching, so that through patience and the consolation of the Scriptures we may have hope.
verses.15:5: Now may the God of patience and comfort grant you to be of the same mind toward one another according to Jesus Christ,
verses.15:6: so that, of one mind and with one mouth, you may honor the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.15:7: For this reason, welcome one another, just as Christ also welcomed you, to the honor of God.
verses.15:8: For I say that Christ Jesus was a minister of the circumcision because of the truth of God, to confirm the promises of the fathers,
verses.15:9: and that the Gentiles honor God on account of mercy, just as it is written: "For this reason I will praise You among the Gentiles, Lord, and I will sing to Your name."
verses.15:10: And again it says: "Rejoice, Gentiles, with His people."
verses.15:11: And again: "Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and magnify Him, all you peoples."
verses.15:12: And again Isaiah says: "There will be the root of Jesse, and He who will rise up to rule the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will hope."
verses.15:13: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope and the power of the Holy Spirit.
verses.15:14: Now I myself also am certain about you, my brothers, that you yourselves also are full of love, filled with all knowledge, so that you are able to admonish one another.
verses.15:15: However, I have written to you rather boldly in part, brothers, as reminding you again, because of the grace that was given to me by God,
verses.15:16: that I may be a minister of Christ Jesus among the Gentiles, sanctifying the gospel of God, so that the offering of the Gentiles may become acceptable and sanctified in the Holy Spirit.
verses.15:17: Therefore I have glory in Christ Jesus toward God.
verses.15:18: For I do not dare to speak anything of those things which Christ does not accomplish through me for the obedience of the Gentiles, by word and deeds,
verses.15:19: in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Holy Spirit, so that from Jerusalem and all around as far as Illyricum I have fulfilled the gospel of Christ.
verses.15:20: And in this way I have preached this gospel, not where Christ was named, so that I would not build upon another's foundation,
verses.15:21: but just as it is written: "Those to whom it has not been announced concerning Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand."
verses.15:22: For this reason also I was greatly hindered from coming to you, and I have been prevented until now.
verses.15:23: But now, having no further place in these regions, and having a longing to come to you already for many preceding years,
verses.15:24: when I begin to set out for Spain, I hope that in passing through I may see you, and be escorted there by you, if first I have enjoyed your company in part.
verses.15:25: Now, therefore, I will set out for Jerusalem to minister to the saints.
verses.15:26: For Macedonia and Achaia have approved making some contribution for the poor among the saints who are in Jerusalem.
verses.15:27: For it pleased them, and they are their debtors. For if the Gentiles have been made sharers of their spiritual things, they ought also to minister to them in material things.
verses.15:28: Therefore, when I have completed this and consigned this fruit to them, I will set out for Spain by way of you.
verses.15:29: Now I know that when I come to you, I will come in the abundance of the blessing of the gospel of Christ.
verses.15:30: Therefore I implore you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Holy Spirit, that you help me in your prayers for me to God,
verses.15:31: that I may be delivered from the unbelievers who are in Judea, and that the offering of my service may become acceptable to the saints in Jerusalem,
verses.15:32: so that I may come to you in joy through the will of God and be refreshed with you.
verses.15:33: Now may the God of peace be with all of you. Amen.
verses.16:1: Now I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, who is in the service of the church that is in Cenchreae,
verses.16:2: that you may welcome her in the Lord as is worthy of the saints, and assist her in whatever matter she may have need of you; for indeed she herself has also assisted many, and me myself.
verses.16:3: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my helpers in Christ Jesus
verses.16:4: (who laid down their own necks for my life, to whom not I alone give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles),
verses.16:5: and the church in their house. Greet Epaenetus, beloved to me, who is the firstfruit of Asia in Christ.
verses.16:6: Greet Mary, who labored much among you.
verses.16:7: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my relatives and fellow prisoners, who are distinguished among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.
verses.16:8: Greet Ampliatus, most beloved to me in the Lord.
verses.16:9: Greet Urbanus, our helper in Christ Jesus, and Stachys, my beloved.
verses.16:11: Greet those who are from the household of Aristobulus. Greet Herodion, my relative. Greet those who are from the household of Narcissus, who are in the Lord.
verses.16:12: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet Persis, dearly loved, who labored much in the Lord.
verses.16:13: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, and mine.
verses.16:14: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brothers who are with them.
verses.16:15: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympias, and all the saints who are with them.
verses.16:16: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.
verses.16:17: Now I ask you, brothers, to keep watch on those who create dissensions and stumbling blocks contrary to the teaching that you learned, and turn away from them.
verses.16:18: For people of this kind do not serve Christ our Lord, but their own belly, and through sweet words and blessings they lead astray the hearts of the innocent.
verses.16:19: For your obedience has been made known in every place. Therefore I rejoice in you. But I want you to be wise in what is good, and simple in what is evil.
verses.16:20: Now may the God of peace crush Satan under your feet quickly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
verses.16:21: Timothy, my helper, greets you, as do Lucius, and Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives.
verses.16:22: I, Tertius, who wrote the letter, greet you in the Lord.
verses.16:23: Gaius, my host, and the whole church greet you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, and Quartus, the brother, greet you.
verses.16:24: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen.
verses.16:25: Now to Him who is able to strengthen you in accordance with my gospel and the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery kept silent for eternal ages
verses.16:26: (which has now been disclosed through the Scriptures of the prophets according to the command of the eternal God, for the obedience of faith), known among all the nations,
verses.16:27: to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.

notes.1:3: The Clementine Vulgate includes "ei" ("for Him"), specifying that the Son was made from David's seed for God; this dative is absent from the Greek text.
notes.1:4: The Vulgate renders the Greek "horisthentos" ("declared" or "designated") as "praedestinatus est" ("was predestined"), a notable Latin reading reflected throughout Western exegesis.
notes.1:17: The Vulgate renders the quotation from Habakkuk 2:4 in the present tense ("vivit", "lives") rather than the Greek future tense ("will live").
notes.1:30: Latin "Deo odibiles" uses a passive adjective with the dative ("hateful to God"), whereas the Greek "theostygeis" is often rendered actively as "haters of God."
notes.1:32: The Clementine Vulgate adds "non intellexerunt" ("they did not understand") and links both those who do such things and those who consent to them as worthy of death, differing from the Greek clause structure.
notes.2:17: The Clementine Vulgate reads "Si autem" ("But if"), matching the Byzantine Greek tradition, whereas modern critical Greek editions read "Ide" ("See"); the Vulgate treats verses 19-20 as the concluding clause of the sentence.
notes.2:21: In the Clementine Vulgate, verses 21-23 are punctuated as direct declarative indictments rather than rhetorical questions.
notes.2:22: The Vulgate renders the Greek "hierosyleis" ("rob temples") more broadly as "sacrilegium facis" ("commit sacrilege").
notes.2:29: Latin "in spiritu, non littera" lacks articles and may refer either to the Holy Spirit or to inward spiritual reality contrasted with the written letter of the law.
notes.3:4: The Vulgate uses the indicative "Est" ("God is true") where the Greek has an imperative ("let God be proved true"), and renders the quotation's final verb passively ("when You are judged"), following the Septuagint.
notes.3:9: Where the debated Greek middle/passive verb can mean "are we better off?" or "are we worse off?", the Vulgate renders it actively with an explicit object, "præcellimus eos" ("do we surpass them?").
notes.3:22: The Vulgate reads "in omnes et super omnes qui credunt in eum" ("to all and upon all who believe in Him"), including "upon all" and "in Him" which are absent from modern critical Greek texts. The genitive "fidem Jesu Christi" can be understood either objectively ("faith in Jesus Christ") or subjectively ("the faithfulness of Jesus Christ").
notes.3:25: The Vulgate renders the rare Greek word "paresis" ("passing over") as "remissionem" ("remission" or "forgiveness").
notes.3:30: The Vulgate uses the present tense "justificat" ("justifies") where the Greek has a future ("will justify"), and preserves the prepositional shift from "ex fide" ("by faith") to "per fidem" ("through faith").
notes.4:5: The concluding clause "secundum propositum gratiæ Dei" ("according to the purpose of the grace of God") is a distinctly Clementine Vulgate reading not present in the Greek text.
notes.4:6: The Vulgate renders the Greek accounting verb with the classical Latin bookkeeping idiom "accepto fert" (literally "enters as received," i.e., "credits").
notes.4:8: The Vulgate uses the perfect indicative "non imputavit" ("has not counted") rather than the emphatic future negation of the Greek ("will never count").
notes.4:19: The Vulgate includes the negation "nec consideravit" ("nor did he consider"), aligning with the Byzantine and Western textual tradition rather than critical Greek editions that omit the negative.
notes.4:25: The Vulgate uses the active verb "resurrexit" ("rose again") where the Greek has a passive verb ("was raised").
notes.5:1: Latin 'habeamus' is a hortatory subjunctive ('let us have'), whereas many modern translations from the Greek adopt the indicative ('we have').
notes.5:2: The Vulgate reads 'gloriae filiorum Dei' ('of the glory of the sons of God'), including 'of the sons' where the standard Greek text reads simply 'the glory of God'.
notes.5:6: The Vulgate renders this verse as a question ('Ut quid enim... mortuus est?'), whereas the standard Greek text is a declarative statement. In 5:8 the Clementine Vulgate also repeats 'secundum tempus' ('at the appointed time') and places 'Christ died for us' at the beginning of 5:9.
notes.5:12: Latin 'in quo' ('in whom', masculine singular referring back to Adam) and 'in hunc mundum' ('into this world') are famous Vulgate readings; the underlying Greek expression is often translated 'because'.
notes.5:16: Latin 'per unum peccatum' ('through one sin') differs from the standard Greek ('through one who sinned'). In 5:17 the Vulgate likewise lists three coordinated genitives ('of grace, and of the gift, and of righteousness').
notes.6:3: The Vulgate uses the ablative 'in morte ipsius' ('in His death') here, contrasting with the accusative 'in mortem' ('into death') in 6:4.
notes.6:5: Latin 'complantati' ('planted together') uses an explicitly botanical metaphor where the Greek term means more broadly 'grown together' or 'united with'.
notes.6:7: Latin 'justificatus est' literally reads 'has been justified' from sin, retaining the same legal verb used in 5:1 and 5:9 rather than 'freed'.
notes.6:23: Latin 'Gratia' translates Greek 'charisma' ('free gift') with the standard term 'grace', contrasting unmerited grace with 'stipendia' ('pay' or military wages).
notes.7:6: The Vulgate reads 'a lege mortis' ('from the law of death'), a notable divergence from the standard Greek text ('from the law, having died to that in which we were held').
notes.7:10: Following the Clementine Vulgate verse division, 'Ego autem mortuus sum' ('I, however, died') opens 7:10 rather than closing 7:9.
notes.7:15: The Vulgate explicitly supplies 'bonum' ('good') and 'malum' ('evil') here, mirroring 7:19, whereas these two nouns are absent from the standard Greek text of 7:15.
notes.7:18: Latin 'non invenio' ('I do not find') reflects the Latin and Byzantine textual tradition, whereas critical Greek editions omit the verb at the end of the clause.
notes.7:25: The Vulgate reads the nominative 'gratia Dei' ('The grace of God') as a direct answer to the question in 7:24, whereas standard Greek editions read 'Thanks be to God'.
notes.8:1: The Vulgate includes the clause qui non secundum carnem ambulant ("who do not walk according to the flesh"), absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts.
notes.8:2: Latin reads first-person singular liberavit me ("has freed me") rather than "you."
notes.8:3: Latin de peccato literally reads "concerning sin" (often understood in context as "for a sin offering").
notes.8:4: Latin justificatio legis literally means "the justification/righteous requirement of the Law."
notes.8:7: Latin shifts from prudentia ("mindset/prudence") in verse 6 to sapientia ("wisdom") here.
notes.8:11: Latin reads Jesum Christum ("Jesus Christ") in the second clause, and propter inhabitantem Spiritum ejus ("because of His Spirit who dwells") uses causal propter rather than instrumental "through."
notes.8:13: The Vulgate reads facta carnis ("the deeds of the flesh") rather than Greek "the deeds of the body."
notes.8:15: Latin preserves the Aramaic address Abba followed by parenthetical (Pater).
notes.8:16: Latin testimonium reddit spiritui nostro uses the dative ("bears witness to our spirit") rather than Greek "with our spirit."
notes.8:18: Latin in nobis reads "in us" rather than "to us."
notes.8:23: The Vulgate explicitly reads adoptionem filiorum Dei ("adoption as sons of God").
notes.8:28: Two distinctive Vulgate features: omnia ("all things") is the subject of cooperantur ("work together"), and vocati sunt sancti adds sancti ("called as saints"). "His" is implied by secundum propositum ("according to the purpose").
notes.8:32: Latin donavit is past/perfect tense ("has He not also freely given") rather than future tense.
notes.8:37: Latin propter eum ("because of Him") is causal rather than instrumental "through Him."
notes.8:38: The Vulgate includes both virtutes ("powers") and fortitudo ("might") in the list.
notes.9:4: The Vulgate reads singular 'testamentum' ("the covenant"), whereas the Greek text reads plural "the covenants."
notes.9:5: The Vulgate's relative clause ('qui est super omnia Deus benedictus') directly identifies Christ as God rather than treating the phrase as an independent doxology.
notes.9:25: The Vulgate includes a third clause from Hosea 2:23 ('et non misericordiam consecutam, misericordiam consecutam') that is absent from most Greek manuscripts of Romans.
notes.9:28: The Vulgate preserves the longer wording from Isaiah 10:23 ('et abbrevians in aequitate: quia verbum breviatum...'), which critical Greek editions shorten.
notes.9:29: The Vulgate retains the Hebrew transliteration 'Sabaoth,' meaning "hosts" or "armies."
notes.10:8: The Vulgate explicitly supplies 'Scriptura' ("Scripture"), where the Greek reads simply "what does it say?", and has 'Prope est verbum' ("The word is near") without "you."
notes.10:15: The Vulgate retains the fuller reading 'evangelizantium pacem, evangelizantium bona' ("who proclaim good news of peace, of those who proclaim good news of good things"), whereas critical Greek editions omit the clause about peace.
notes.10:16: Latin 'auditus' ("report" here, "hearing" in 10:17) forms a direct verbal link between Isaiah's question and Paul's conclusion in the next verse.
notes.10:21: The Vulgate reads 'non credentem' ("unbelieving") where the Greek text reads 'apeithounta' ("disobedient").
notes.11:5: The Vulgate reads 'salvæ factæ sunt' ('has been saved'), whereas the Greek text has 'gegonen' ('has come to be' or 'exists').
notes.11:7: The Vulgate renders Greek 'eporothesan' ('were hardened') as 'excæcati sunt' ('were blinded'), and similarly translates 'porosis' ('hardening') as 'cæcitas' ('blindness') in 11:25.
notes.11:8: Latin 'spiritum compunctionis' literally means 'a spirit of compunction' (or 'pricking'), a formal rendering of Greek 'pneuma katanyxeos' ('a spirit of stupor' or 'numbness') via the shared root sense of pricking or piercing.
notes.11:32: In 11:30-32 the Vulgate renders Greek 'apeitheia' ('disobedience') with 'incredulitas' ('unbelief') and 'non credere' ('not believe'), and here uses the neuter plural 'omnia' ('all things') where the Greek has masculine 'tous pantas' ('all people').
notes.11:36: The Vulgate reads 'in ipso' ('in Him') in the third prepositional phrase, where the Greek text reads 'eis auton' ('to Him').
notes.12:1: Latin misericordiam is singular ("mercy"), and rationabile obsequium literally means "reasonable service" or "rational worship."
notes.12:2: Latin reformamini in novitate sensus vestri literally means "be reformed in the newness of your mind/understanding."
notes.12:11: The Vulgate reads Domino servientes ("serving the Lord") rather than the variant "serving the time."
notes.12:17: The Vulgate includes non tantum coram Deo, sed etiam ("not only before God, but also"), reflecting an expanded textual tradition.
notes.12:19: Latin non vosmetipsos defendentes literally means "not defending/avenging yourselves."
notes.13:8: The Vulgate reads 'proximum' ('neighbor') here, aligning with 13:9-10, where the Greek text has 'ton heteron' ('the other').
notes.13:9: The Clementine Vulgate includes 'non falsum testimonium dices' ('you shall not give false testimony'), a clause attested in some Greek manuscripts and the Byzantine tradition but omitted in modern critical Greek editions.
notes.13:10: Latin 'Dilectio proximi' uses the genitive ('love of one's neighbor'), whereas the Greek text uses the dative ('to plesion', 'does no wrong to a neighbor').
notes.14:2: The Clementine Vulgate reads the jussive subjunctive 'manducet' ('let him eat') rather than the indicative ('eats') found in the Greek.
notes.14:5: Latin 'judicat diem inter diem' literally means 'judges day between day' (distinguishing one day from another, while another regards every day alike). 'In suo sensu abundet' literally means 'let him abound in his own mind,' expressing full personal conviction.
notes.14:14: Latin 'commune' literally means 'common' (i.e., ritually unclean or profane). Vulgate 'per ipsum' ('through Him') naturally refers to Christ, whereas the Greek 'di heautou' means 'in itself.'
notes.14:16: The Vulgate reads 'bonum nostrum' ('our good') rather than the Greek 'your good'; similarly, it reads 'Deus' ('God') in 14:4 and 'Christi' ('of Christ') in 14:10 where critical Greek editions read 'Lord' and 'God,' and adds 'custodiamus' ('let us guard') in 14:19.
notes.14:23: Latin 'discernit' literally means 'distinguishes' or 'makes a distinction' (having scruples over foods), rendering the Greek middle participle 'diakrinomenos' ('doubting').
notes.15:2: The Clementine Vulgate reads 'vestrum' ('of you') rather than the Greek 'of us.'
notes.15:13: The Vulgate coordinates 'in spe, et virtute Spiritus Sancti' ('in hope and the power of the Holy Spirit') with 'et' ('and'), whereas the Greek reads 'in hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.'
notes.15:14: The Clementine Vulgate reads 'dilectione' ('love') where the Greek text reads 'agathosynes' ('goodness').
notes.15:20: The Vulgate reads 'praedicavi Evangelium hoc' ('I have preached this gospel') rather than the Greek 'making it my ambition to preach the gospel'; in 15:16 'sanctificans' ('sanctifying') likewise renders the Greek 'serving as a priest of.'
notes.15:22: The clause 'et prohibitus sum usque adhuc' ('and I have been prevented until now') is a Vulgate-distinct addition not in the Greek; similarly, in 15:31 'obsequii mei oblatio' ('the offering of my service') expands the Greek 'my service.'
notes.16:15: The Clementine Vulgate reads the feminine name Olympiadem ("Olympias"), whereas the Greek text has the masculine name Olympan ("Olympas").
notes.16:18: Latin benedictiones ("blessings," literally "fair words") translates Greek eulogia, which in this context carries the sense of flattery or smooth praise.
notes.16:20: The Vulgate uses the optative subjunctive conterat ("may [He] crush"), expressing a prayerful wish where the Greek text has the future indicative ("will crush").
notes.16:23: The Vulgate places universa ecclesia ("the whole church") in the nominative as a co-sender of the greeting, whereas the Greek has the genitive ("host to me and to the whole church").
notes.16:27: The Vulgate reads honor et gloria ("honor and glory"), where the Greek text has only "glory," and retains the relative pronoun cui ("to whom").
